metadata.title: Systems, Surroundings And Boundaries
metadata.topic: Thermodynamic system definitions for the first foundation lesson

learningPurpose: Give students a focused, source-linked vocabulary for selecting and classifying a thermodynamic system before equations or property data are introduced.

definitions.meaning: The selected matter or region chosen for a thermodynamic analysis.
Everything outside the selected system for the stated analysis.
The real or imagined surface that separates the system from its surroundings.
A fixed quantity of matter selected for analysis; mass does not cross its boundary.
A selected region in space whose boundary may be crossed by mass.
A system that does not exchange matter or energy with its surroundings.
A measurable characteristic used to describe a system.
The condition of a system described by its properties at an instant.
A change by which a system moves from one state to another.
A sequence of processes that returns a system to its initial state.
A property whose value does not depend on the amount of matter selected.
A property whose value depends on the amount of matter selected.

governingPrinciples: Declare the selected system and boundary before deciding which interactions must be tracked.
Classify a system from what may cross the selected boundary, not from the name of the device alone.
Treat property and state vocabulary as preparation for later reviewed equations and property-data lessons.
siUnitNote: This classification topic introduces no numerical calculation or property value; SI units are added only in later source-reviewed lessons.
assumptions: The analysis boundary is selected for the stated learning question.
A sealed classroom container is treated as a closed system only for the stated classification exercise.
No property values, equilibrium criteria, or process equations are inferred.
limitations: Does not introduce steam, refrigerant, material, or other property data.
Does not establish heat, work, mass-flow, or energy-balance equations.
Does not teach equilibrium criteria, equipment ratings, operating limits, or design rules.
The Purdue notes are concise course material rather than a complete property-data authority.

workedExample.title: Classify a sealed classroom container
workedExample.purpose: Practise declaring a system boundary and classifying whether mass may cross it.
given: A sealed rigid container is selected as the system.
The container wall is selected as the boundary.
steps: Name the matter inside the selected system.
Identify everything outside the boundary as surroundings.
Decide whether mass may cross the sealed boundary.
workedExample.answer: For this exercise, the sealed contents form a closed system because mass does not cross the selected boundary.

normalOperation: Learners declare the system and boundary before classifying the system or discussing interactions.
commonMisconceptions: Treating the physical device name as the system definition without stating a boundary.
Assuming every sealed system is isolated.
Calling a property intensive or extensive without considering whether it depends on the amount of matter.
Starting a calculation before the system and boundary are declared.

faultConditions.title: Unstated or inconsistent boundary
symptoms: The learner cannot decide whether mass crosses the boundary.
The selected system changes partway through the explanation.
likelyCauses: The system boundary was not declared before classification.
faultConditions.safeResponse: Return to the definition step, state the selected system and boundary, and then repeat the classification.

safety.warning: System classification alone does not establish equipment operating limits, pressure limits, or thermal safety controls.
safety.studentBoundary: Students must not infer permission to operate, open, heat, pressurise, or design real equipment from this introductory lesson.
